scope: Experimental optional entity TiKV backend. No performance equivalence to JuiceFS is claimed.

semantics.scope: Experimental entity packed lower + TiKV upper vs stock JuiceFS 1.3.1 + TiKV. Redis entity native/packed regression guards use current main cba857b with the same upstream packed improvements as the candidate.

workload.packed_layout: Current-main producer cba857b; size-only frame policy; random-small-file profile with 256 KiB default maximum raw frame; inline data off; 4 MiB chunk/block geometry. Exact producer hash is recorded in baseline-build.json and cloud runtime provenance.

semantics.topology: One task-owned spot VM, one PD and one TiKV with one replica, RustFS, identical loopback nginx byte-counting proxy for all clients. Not an HA or remote-latency claim.
semantics.timing: Report active, debt-observation, drain/unmount/maintenance/process-exit tail, active+tail, and complete prewarm-inclusive interval. Packing, JuiceFS corpus import, mount and workload preparation separately recorded.
semantics.writeback_semantics: BrewFS fsync acknowledges a durable local spool; pinned JuiceFS writeback staging closes and renames its file without an explicit fsync in that path. Compare remote-complete totals; do not call foreground acknowledgement guarantees identical.

observations: flushPage writes data/checksum, closes and renames; no explicit f.Sync or directory sync in this path
Prior pinned cached_store.go inspection shows writeback staging success is returned before remote upload

configuration_caveats: The pre-existing local pingcap/pd:v8.5.0 and pingcap/tikv:v8.5.0 aliases actually contain version 8.5.3. Exact local images are exported to the cloud; binary version output, filesystem/runtime-configuration fingerprints and archive hashes are verified. No claim of testing 8.5.0 is made.

Application workers are eight. JuiceFS explicitly limits uploads to eight; this pinned version has no max-downloads CLI flag. BrewFS entity background PUT concurrency is eight. BrewFS S3 max_concurrency is explicitly eight but controls multipart parts, not a global download queue; these workloads use objects below its default 16 MiB multipart threshold. Internal request scheduling is not claimed identical.
JuiceFS cache-size=0 disables writeback. Synchronous/read-only cells use 0; asynchronous cells use the minimum positive 1B to enable staging, with no complete clean data block retained.

BrewFS retains a 64 MiB immutable metadata memo, a 4 MiB index cache, and current-main authenticated group/frame-directory caches capped at 256/128 KiB for this index budget. Payload caches remain off. Metadata cache implementations are not identical.
Matching prewarm and random traces does not establish a 50% steady cache-hit rate.
BrewFS authenticates packed payload frames; JuiceFS range reads can use a smaller transfer and different integrity work. Object GET bytes are measured rather than assumed.
Default Redis guards use one Tokio worker on both binaries; TiKV comparison explicitly uses eight runtime workers on both clients without changing product defaults.

Each timed cell starts a fresh filesystem mount. Cold-small-read means no explicit application prewarm, not cold server storage. The TiKV/RustFS and server OS caches are not flushed between cells; fixed corpus, paired alternating order and repeated samples are used.
semantics.baseline_change: R6 used 060db0d and was rejected in the small-write pilot because the unlocked allocator counter read could starve its CAS loop. R7 uses main cba857b for both BrewFS arms and the producer, with the candidate adding locked atomic entity allocations. Corpus, operation traces, workers, upload modes, cache configuration and complete drain accounting remain unchanged. R6 pilot times are not accepted comparison results.
semantics.harness_rerun: Only ordinary EBUSY is retried, within five seconds, with every attempt recorded. All primary-cell retry time remains inside measured drain. No force/lazy unmount. Full 214-cell rerun after R7 stopped at the JuiceFS verification unmount; no partial sample reuse.
